baseline.text: How do mansard roofs and domes both serve shelter, yet through different structural and formal strategies?

options.text: Mansard roofs shed water efficiently; domes shed water poorly and require central drainage, especially in regions with high rainfall
Mansard roofs are decorative elements; domes are purely structural, often used in monumental architecture to symbolize grandeur
Both use pitched slopes to prevent water pooling; both use arches to distribute loads, although domes achieve this through a continuous curved surface
Mansard roofs create additional attic space; domes create open interior space by spanning large openings without interior columns

rationale.a: Domes (like Pantheon) shed water effectively through slope; the comparison is false.
rationale.b: Both are highly functional structural elements, not decorative.
rationale.c: Domes use curvature and load distribution (outward/downward), not pitched water-shedding slopes like mansards.
rationale.correct: Mansards provide shelter through additional enclosed volume (historically for tax-exempt attics); domes provide shelter by spanning large circular openings with elegant curved vaults—both shelter strategies but structurally and spatially distinct.

title: lea-theo-002-01-core-concept

baseline.text: A cortile is best defined as:

options.text: A covered walkway with columns supporting a roof, protecting circulation from weather
A public civic square surrounded by important buildings and serving as gathering space
An internal courtyard surrounded by covered arcaded walkways on all four sides
A raised platform in a church from which the clergy delivers sermons

rationale.a: That is an arcade or portico—a circulation element, not a complete courtyard system.
rationale.b: That is a piazza—a public external civic square, not an internal palace courtyard.
rationale.d: That is a pulpit—a church element unrelated to courtyards.
rationale.correct: A cortile is specifically an internal courtyard (characteristic of Italian Renaissance palaces) surrounded by arcaded covered walkways on all sides, providing light, air, semi-private circulation, and social space.
